1988 C L C 442

[Lahore]

Before Amjad Khan, J

MUHAMMAD RAMZANâ€‘â€‘Petitioner

versus

ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE III,
BAHAWALPUR

and anotherâ€‘â€‘Respondents.

Writ Petition No.3â€‘F of
1986/BWP, decided on 7th March, 1987

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)â€‘â€‘

â€‘â€‘â€‘S 14â€‘â€‘Constitution of Pakistan
(1973) , Art 199 Constitutional jurisdiction against finding of Appellate Court
whereby petitioner's appeal against decree for jactitation of marriage was
dismissed on assumption that such Court had no jurisdiction in the matterâ€‘ Constitutional
jurisdiction being discretionary in nature, its exercise was regulated largely
by facts and circumstances of a dispute, and cannot be exercised in disregard
thereof, and not even as a matter of mere courseâ€‘â€‘Even where
impugned order was found to be illegal, constitutional jurisdiction could not
be invoked if such order was found to be just and proper oneâ€‘â€‘Although
petitioner's appeal against, decree for jactitation of marriage was
maintainable under S.14 of Act XXXV of 1964, inasmuch as same does not fall
within exclusion class thereof, yet case against petitioner having been decided
by a Court of competent jurisdiction on merits, and such decision not shown to
be either unjust and improper on record, case for exercise of constitutional
jurisdiction against same could not be made out.

Nawab Syed Raunaq Ali etc. v.
Chief Settlement Commissioner and others P L D 1973 S C 236; Begum Shamsâ€‘unâ€‘Nisa
v. Said Akbar Abbasi and another 1982 S C M R 413 and Rehmat Ullah and Mst.
Hameeda Begum and others 1986 S C M R 1561 rel.

Rana Muhammad Yaqoob Khan for
Petitioner.

ORDER

A suit for jactitation of
marriage filed by Mst. Sughran Bibi respondent No.2 was decreed by the Family
Judge, Ahmadpur East by his judgment dated 1â€‘10â€‘1986. Petitioner
filed an appeal there against in the District Court at Bahawalpur which was dismissed
by a learned Additional District Judge on 9â€‘12â€‘1986 on the
assumption that it was not competent under Section 14 of the Punjab Family
Courts Act, 1964.

2. The defendant seeks the aid of
this Court to assail the appellate order in this writ petition which, however,
is not accompanied by either a copy of the judgment passed against him by the
Family Court or that of the evidence led in the suit.

3. Writ jurisdiction is
discretionary in nature and its exercise is regulated largely by the facts and
circumstances of a dispute so that it is not open to be exercised in disregard
thereof and not even as a matter of mere course. Petitioner has not even
detailed the facts of the controversy in his petition to apprise this Court
either of the justness of his claim or even to canvass impropriety of the
judgment passed by the trial Court on the basis of the evidence which may have
been led by the parties. Reference may be made to Nawab Syed Raunaq Ali etc. v.
Chief Settlement Commissioner and others P L D 1973 S C 236, Begum Shamsâ€‘unâ€‘Nisa
v. Said Akbar Abbasi and another 1982 S C M R 413 and Rehmat Ullah and others
v. Mst. Hameeda Begum and others 1986 S C M R 1561 for the proposition that
even if an impugned order is found to be illegal, writ may not issue if the
order may be a just and proper one. Although it is correct that the
petitioner's appeal to the District Court against the decree for jactitation of
marriage was maintainable under Section 14 of the Punjab Familyâ€‘Courts
Act, 1964 inasmuch as such an appeal does not fall within the exclusionâ€‘clause
thereof, yet, since a Court of competent jurisdiction has decided the case
against the petitioner on merits to hold him to be an impositor and he has not
shown that judgment to be either unjust or improper on the record and muchless
has he made out a case about his being just for being granted relief against
it, therefore, writ cannot issue at his instance. No case at all for exercise
of constitutional jurisdiction can be held to have been made out on the present
record.

4. The Writ Petition has no force is accordingly dismissed in
limine.

dismissed.
